title: Book 7 — Polymnia, Chapter 172
paragraphs: As for the Thessalians, at first they had taken the side of the Persians unwillingly, and they gave proof that they were not pleased with what the Aleuadae were plotting. For as soon as they heard that the Persian was about to cross over into Europe, they sent envoys to the Isthmus; at the Isthmus were assembled representatives of Greece chosen by those cities that had the better mind for Greece. Coming before these men, the Thessalian envoys said: “Greeks, you must guard the pass by Olympus, so that Thessaly and all Greece may be sheltered from the war. We are prepared to join you in guarding it, but you must send a large force as well; for if you do not, know well that we shall come to terms with the Persian. It is not right that we, standing as outposts so far in advance of the rest of Greece, should perish alone in your defense. And if you are unwilling to come to our aid, you cannot apply any force against us to compel us to do the impossible; rather we shall try to devise some means of safety for ourselves.”
